routes.name: Enafors → Duved
routes.sub: Enan, Ånnsjön and the tarn chain
routes.yours: You skated this on 3 Dec 2022: 50.9 km, 6 h 36 min moving. Clear ice with some snow on top, no open water.

out.text: Norrtåg westbound to Enafors. Only 2 trains a day stop there, so take the morning one.
Weekdays: bus 571 leaves Duved at 06:00 and 13:50 towards Enafors. The 06:00 works for a pre-dawn start in November.

back.text: Leave the ice where Greningen ends and walk about 3 km down into Duved, past Forsaforsen.
From Duved: Norrtåg about 4 a day, or bus 157 to Åre/Undersåker/Järpen roughly every hour, every day.

hazards: Enanfors waterfall is right next to Enafors station. Get on the ice below it.
The Enan is river ice: thinner over the current and on the outside of bends. Its mouth into Ånnsjön is shallow and sandy.
Kärrån is a stream. Watch for springs and soft spots. Your track avoided Ånnsjön's outlet at Ånn, which is often open.
Greningen is a regulated reservoir. The water level moves, so expect cracks and slush along the shore.

spots.name: Enanfors waterfall
spots.text: Open water at the falls next to Enafors station. Get on the Enan below them.

spots.name: Kärrån
spots.text: km 21–28 on your 2022 trip: 2–4 km/h with a 49 min stop. Mostly slow skating on poor stream ice, with some walking.

spots.name: Kösjön → Rängen → Moen
spots.text: km 34–40: 3–5 km/h. Slow skating through the small tarns, with walking between them.

spots.name: Moen → Greningen
spots.text: km 41–48: 2–5 km/h, Greningen included. Slow skating on poor ice, with some walking.

spots.name: Down to Duved
spots.text: km 48–51: a steady 5 km/h. You walked home from here, past Forsaforsen.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

routes.name: Enafors → Ånn
routes.sub: Down the Enan and across Ånnsjön

out.text: Norrtåg westbound to Enafors in the morning.

back.text: Norrtåg eastbound from Ånn, which also has 2 trains a day. With the autumn timetable that meant an evening train.
Weekdays: bus 571 eastbound from Storlien at 14:55 and 17:10 passes Ånn (exact time at Ånn unverified).

hazards: Enanfors waterfall is next to the station, so start below it.
River ice on the Enan, and a shallow, sandy mouth.
Ånnsjön's outlet east of Ånn (around 63.314, 12.605) is often open water with swans. Leave the ice at the station shore, not at the outlet.
routes.note: Enaforsholm sells a guided 9 km Enan–Ånnsjön tour, so the Enan section is known skating.

spots.name: Enanfors waterfall
spots.text: Open water at the falls next to Enafors station. Get on the Enan below them.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

routes.name: Ånn → Duved
routes.sub: Your tarn chain without the Enan, train at both ends

out.text: Norrtåg westbound to Ånn in the morning (2 trains a day).
Weekdays: bus 571 from Duved at 06:00 or 13:50 to Ånn.

back.text: Leave Greningen and walk about 3 km down into Duved.
Norrtåg from Duved (about 4 a day) or bus 157 roughly every hour.

hazards: Leave Ånn heading south-east along the shore, and stay well away from the outlet east of Ånn.
Kärrån and the gaps between the tarns were slow in 2022: some skating, some walking.
Greningen is a regulated reservoir, so expect cracks along the shore.
routes.note: This is the same chain you skated in 2022, minus the first 21 km. With train stations at both ends, you don't need the early train to Enafors.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

spots.name: Kärrån
spots.text: Slow in 2022: 2–4 km/h, a mix of skating on poor stream ice and walking.

spots.name: Kösjön → Rängen → Moen
spots.text: Slow in 2022 (3–5 km/h): skating through the small tarns, with walking between them.

spots.name: Moen → Greningen
spots.text: Slow in 2022 (2–5 km/h): poor ice and some walking.

routes.name: Klocka loop: Enan and south Ånnsjön
routes.sub: An SLSK club tour, 23 Dec 2025 (42 km)

out.text: Park at Klocka on the north-west shore of Ånnsjön (about 30 min from Åre).

back.text: Back to Klocka. It's a loop, so you only need one car.

hazards: Keep out from the sandbanks at the Enan mouth.
The Enan is river ice, so it's thinner over the current and on the outside of bends.
South of Granön and Järpön, Ånnsjön freezes later than the north part.
routes.note: In Dec 2025, SLSK and Friluftsfrämjandet went Klocka → Enan mouth → Enafors → a bit up Ingolvån → south Ånnsjön → Klocka, 42 km (trip report). One utsidan poster also suggests Klocka as the place to start when you're unsure about the ice.

spots.name: Enan mouth sandbanks
spots.text: Shallow and sandy. Ice can be poor here, so keep out from the banks.

spots.name: Enanfors waterfall
spots.text: Turn around below the falls by Enafors.

routes.name: Ånn → Ottsjö
routes.sub: Kärrån, Kösjön, the Gräpplingen tarns and Ottsjön

out.text: Norrtåg westbound to Ånn in the morning.

back.text: Bus 562 from Ottsjö to Undersåker, then train or bus 157. Weekdays it leaves Vålådalen at 06:50, 10:00 and 14:20 (the 15:10 and 17:10 skip Ottsjö village). Weekends 10:00, 15:00 and 18:35. It reaches Ottsjö about 15 min later (unverified).

hazards: Kärrån is stream ice. You skated it in 2022, but its condition varies from year to year.
There is no mapped stream between Kösjön and Stentjärnen, so expect about 3 km on foot through snow. Bring skate guards or boots.
Skårrån falls about 6 km down to Ottsjön. Whether it can be skated is unknown, so be ready to walk it.
Ridvadet is a shallow ford across Ottsjön at Ottsjö village and may have weak ice (unverified).
routes.note: This is the second half of your Vålådalen idea, and it works on its own as a train-out, bus-home day.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

spots.name: Kärrån
spots.text: Stream ice. On your 2022 trip this stretch went at walking pace, 2–4 km/h.

spots.name: Skårrån
spots.text: A stream falling about 6 km to Ottsjön. It is unknown whether it can be skated, so be ready to walk all of it.

spots.name: Ridvadet ford, Ottsjön
spots.text: A shallow ford (under 40 cm deep) across the lake from Ottsjö village. Ice may be weak here. Position approximate, unverified.

routes.name: Vålådalen → Ånnsjön → Ottsjö
routes.sub: Your idea: Nulltjärnarna, down Rekån, back along the tarn chain

out.text: Bus 562 from Undersåker to Vålådalen: weekdays 08:00, Sat 08:00, Sun 08:45. Then about 3.5 km on foot to Nulltjärnarna.

back.text: Bus 562 from Ottsjö back to Undersåker (see the Ånn → Ottsjö route), or leave a car at Sjöändan.

hazards: There is no lake called Ånnsjön near Vålådalen. The only Ånnsjön is the big one at Ånn, so this route goes all the way there via Rekån.
Rekån is a 27 km mountain stream. Small inflows freeze early, but rapids, springs and snow bridges are all possible. Nobody has reported skating its upper part.
About 60 km with roughly 10 km on foot is a very long day, around 8–9 hours even on good ice. Headlamps handle the dark, but early-season snow and stream ice will set the pace.
This is remote ground with poor phone coverage away from Ånnsjön. Don't go alone.
routes.note: Nulltjärnarna on its own is a classic early-ice tarn. Bus 562 out and back makes a short first-ice day.

spots.name: Rekån
spots.text: A 27 km mountain stream. Expect rapids, springs and snow bridges. Nobody has reported skating it, so assume some walking.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

spots.text: A stream falling about 6 km to Ottsjön. It is unknown whether it can be skated, so be ready to walk all of it.

routes.name: Ånnsjön grand loop
routes.sub: Out-and-back across Ånnsjön and up the Enan
routes.yours: You skated this on 20 Nov 2022: 46.8 km in 3 h 17 min moving, about 14 km/h on good ice.

out.text: Drive to the west shore of Ånnsjön (your start point on the map), or take the train to Ånn and add 2–3 km.

back.text: Back to the car. A loop needs no shuttle.

hazards: The north part is shallow and freezes first. Ice south of Granön and Järpön comes later.
A sound on the north-shore route is known for thin ice.
Open water at the outlet by Ånn.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

routes.name: Ånn shore laps
routes.sub: Your regular short sessions from Ånn
routes.yours: You've done four of these between 2020 and 2023, 8–20 km each.

out.text: Park at Ånn. By train you'd arrive in the morning and leave in the evening, so it's a full day.

back.text: Back to the car.

hazards: Open water at the outlet east of Ånn.
Thin ice in the sound on the north shore.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

routes.name: Handöl → Ånn

out.text: Two cars: leave one at Ånn and drive about 15 min to Handöl.
Weekdays: bus 571 serves Handöl Hanriis, but the detour into Handöl must be booked (call 0771-82 00 83 by 16:00 the weekday before).

back.text: From Ånn: the car, the evening Norrtåg, or a weekday bus 571.

hazards: The southern part freezes later than the north. Check the ice off Handöl first.
Open water at the outlet by Ånn.
routes.note: A short, easy option with two cars, and good for a first session of the season.

spots.name: Ånnsjön outlet at Ånn
spots.text: Often open water with swans where Ånnsjön drains east. Keep well clear.

routes.name: Ottsjön end to end
routes.yours: You did a short skate at Sjöändan on 26 Nov 2022.

out.text: Two cars: park one in Ottsjö and drive to Sjöändan (about 10 km from the Undersåker bridge).
Or use bus 562 to Ottsjö and skate out-and-back.

back.text: Collect the car in Ottsjö, or take bus 562 back to Undersåker.

hazards: Ottsjön is unregulated: regulation was refused in 1956. That usually means steadier ice than the reservoirs.
Ridvadet is a shallow ford across the lake from Ottsjö village and may have weak ice (unverified).
Inflows from the Vålån (south shore) and Skårrån (west end) can mean soft ice near their mouths.

spots.name: Vålån inflow
spots.text: River mouth. Ice is often soft or thin near inflows.

spots.name: Skårrån inflow
spots.text: Stream mouth at the west end. Soft ice possible.

spots.name: Ridvadet ford
spots.text: A shallow ford across the lake from Ottsjö village. Ice may be weak here. Position approximate, unverified.

routes.note: SLSK ran an early-December club tour here with about 23 skaters. Their tips: put in at the boat harbour just after ICA Ottsjö, and "passa för sand vid ridvadet" (SLSK Iskontakten).

routes.name: Järpen → Mörsil

out.text: Norrtåg or bus 157 to Järpen. The station is about 100 m from the shore.

back.text: Leave the ice at the east end and walk about 2.5 km to Mörsil station.
Norrtåg (4–5 a day) or bus 157 (roughly hourly).

hazards: Järpströmmen carries the outflow from the Kallsjön power station into Liten at Järpen. Expect open or thin water near the start, so go out well away from the inflow (unverified).
The Indalsälven flows through Liten, and it's probably regulated by the Mörsil dam, so watch for current lines and shore cracks.
routes.note: This is the easiest trip to reach by public transport. It's short, so it suits an afternoon.

spots.name: Järpströmmen and Indalsälven inflow
spots.text: Outflow from the Kallsjön power station and the Indalsälven both enter the west end. Expect open or thin water. Position approximate.

routes.name: Huså → Kall → Bonäset

out.text: Two cars: leave one at Bonäset and drive to Huså.
Weekdays: bus 553 from Järpen reaches Huså at about 08:00 (booked trip) and 15:55.

back.text: Collect the car at Bonäset. Bus 551/553 passes Bonäshamn on weekdays.

hazards: Kallsjön is a deep (134 m), regulated reservoir. It freezes late, and you get cracks and slush along the shores.
It's very exposed to wind, so watch out for open leads and drifting snow.
routes.note: Reported: Kall–Huså, about 18 km on "30 cm kärnis", 7 Feb 2014 (Dan Fritzon, SLSK Iskontakten).

routes.name: Kallsjön lengthwise

out.text: Two cars: leave one at Kallsedet (about 70 min from Åre) and drive to Huså (about 30 min). You can shorten it by ending at Konäs or Skagen.
Weekdays: bus 551 runs Kallsedet–Konäs–Kall-Rör–Kall–Järpen on a school-run timetable.

back.text: Collect the car at Kallsedet.

hazards: Kallsjön is regulated, which leaves broken slabs and cracks along the shores. Get on and off where it looks calm.
The north part freezes late, often not until January, so plan this for February or March.
Juvuln's power station empties into the very north tip at Kallsedet. Expect thin or open water there and finish on the shore before the outlet (unverified).
It's a huge, open lake, so wind decides the day.
routes.note: Reports: Per Sonnvik skated 55 km in a loop from Skagen on 15 Feb 2025, on smooth ice that was thinner with many cracks at Skagen (trip report). On 29 Feb 2020 someone skated about 30 km north from Huså on 10 cm of clear ice (SLSK Iskontakten).

spots.name: Juvuln outflow, Kallsedet
spots.text: Outflow from Juvelns power station into the north tip. Probably open or thin water (unverified).

spots.name: Anjan outflow, NW arm
spots.text: Water from Anjan enters near Sundet. Keep clear (unverified).

routes.name: Juvuln end to end

out.text: Two cars: leave one at the road by the east end and start at the Kallsedet dam (about 70 min from Åre).
Weekdays: bus 551 stops at Kallsedet and Kolåsen.

back.text: Collect the car at the east end. The road access comes from OSM and is unverified.

hazards: Juvuln is regulated (dam since 1941) and the drawdown is unknown, so expect a broken shore zone.
Avoid the dam and power-station end at Kallsedet itself, and get on a little east of it.
Snowmobile trails cross the lake (VÄSEK: Kallsedet–Kyrkstigen and Bottenleden).
There are no skating reports for this lake. Treat it as unknown ice.
routes.note: Freezes late (median 8 Dec, SMHI), so it suits mid-winter, when the lower lakes are snowed over. You can check the water level daily on Fortum's Juvelns kraftverk page.

spots.name: Juvuln dam and power station
spots.text: Intake and dam. Stay away, and get on the ice further east.

routes.name: Anjan end to end

out.text: Two cars: leave one at Anjehem by the dam (about 65 min from Åre) and drive to road 336 on the west shore (about 80 min).
Weekdays: bus 551 serves Anjan and Sundet.

back.text: Collect the car at Anjehem.

hazards: The level can vary by up to 9.2 m (regulated since 1940), so the shores will be tilted and broken. Pick your way on and off carefully.
Avoid the dam and intake at Anjehem.
Stor-Rensjön drains in at the west end via Vukumanån, so watch for soft ice near the inflow.
There are no skating reports for this lake. Treat it as unknown ice.
routes.note: Long, narrow and remote. You can check the water level on Fortum's Anjans kraftverk page.

spots.name: Anjehem dam
spots.text: Dam and intake. Keep clear.

spots.name: Vukumanån inflow
spots.text: Inflow from Stor-Rensjön, where soft ice is possible. Position approximate.

routes.name: Åre → Brattland

out.text: Start at Åre station, which is about 150 m from the ice.

back.text: Bus 157 from Brattland or Så back to Åre runs roughly every hour, every day.
Or use two cars: Så/Brattland is about 8 min from Åre.

hazards: The Indalsälven flows through the lake, so expect current and weaker ice at the inflow (west) and the outlet (east).
Ice-rally and snowmobile tracks can make the surface rough.
routes.note: New Year's Eve 2014: "åkbar från Åre till Brattland" (SLSK Iskontakten). On 22 Nov 2013 the ice was good but covered in rime frost (blog). It's short, but you can step out of your door and go, which suits an evening session.

spots.name: Indalsälven outlet
spots.text: Current where the river leaves the lake. Expect thinner ice. Position approximate.

routes.name: Gevsjön loop

out.text: Park by the E14 at the east end, or at Tångböle on the west end (about 25 min from Åre).
Weekdays: bus 571 stops at Gevsjön.

back.text: Back to the car.

hazards: Gevsjön is shallow and freezes early, so it's often the first lake that can be skated.
River current at both ends, from Bodsjöströmmen in and the outflow towards Bodsjön.
Two skaters went through the ice on the first Advent weekend in 2022 (Sveriges Radio). Check the ice carefully early in the season.
routes.note: One of the most popular lakes in Åre kommun, according to are.se and aresweden.com.

spots.name: Inflow, west end
spots.text: Bodsjöströmmen enters here. Current means thin ice. Position approximate.

spots.name: Outflow, east end
spots.text: Where the river leaves for Bodsjön. Current means thin ice. Position approximate.

routes.name: Helgesjön loop
routes.sub: Three linked lakes north of Undersåker

out.text: Park on the road along the north side (about 40 min from Åre).

back.text: Back to the car.

hazards: Regulated by a dam at the south-east end (63.340, 13.312), so expect some shore cracks.
Watch for small holes where meltwater has run down (reported 1 Jan 2015).
routes.note: Several good reports: "Fantastisk is på Helgesjön (3 st sammanlänkade sjöar)… solid över hela sjösystemet" (22 Nov 2014), and "Fantastiska isar" (1 Jan 2015), both from SLSK Iskontakten. On 22 Nov 2013 it had totally clear new ice. are.se recommends it too.

spots.name: Helgesjön dam
spots.text: Dam at the outlet. Keep clear.

routes.name: Medstugusjön
routes.sub: Unregulated border lake that freezes early

out.text: Drive road 322 (Skalstuguvägen) to the lake, about 45 min from Åre.

back.text: Back to the car.

hazards: Small (8 km²) but unregulated, so the ice should be even.
There are no skating reports. At 536 m it's exposed to wind and early snow.
routes.note: A good first-ice check before the bigger lakes. SMHI has an active ice station here (median freeze-up 14 Nov).

morsil.name: Mörsil
morsil.why: 420 m, by Liten and nearest to south Kallsjön. Mörsil only reports 2–3 readings a day, so its daily mean is rougher
